studies.label: Classroom experiment: randomized round-two AI switching within each round-one group

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 44), Section 3.1, analyzed sample
counts_source.quote: 분석에 포함된 참여자는 총 164명이며, 1차 조건은 A 83 명, B 81명으로 구성되었다. 2차 조건은 A1 43명, A2 40명, B1 41명, B2 40명이다.

arms.name: A1 (maintain AI)
arms.description: Generative AI available in both rounds; randomly assigned within the round-one AI group to keep AI during the upgrade.

arms.name: A2 (discontinue AI)
arms.description: Generative AI available in round one, removed in round two; randomly assigned within the round-one AI group to upgrade the existing AI-assisted draft without AI. The generative_ai arm code records prior exposure.

arms.name: B1 (adopt AI)
arms.description: No AI in round one; randomly assigned within the round-one no-AI group to adopt generative AI during the upgrade.

arms.name: B2 (maintain no AI)
arms.description: No AI in either round; randomly assigned within the round-one no-AI group to continue the upgrade without AI.

studies.task: Students in IT-related university courses proposed ideas to improve life in 2035, then revised, supplemented, or elaborated their own initial ideas during a second round in the same session.

ai_tool.name: ChatGPT (Free plan, default access at the time); other generative AI tools were also permitted
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 44), Section 3.1, opening paragraph

preregistration.where: No preregistration or registry is mentioned in the document.

estimates.outcome: Gain in total creativity score from round one to round two (H3)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two independent raters blinded to condition scored each idea for novelty, usefulness/feasibility, elaboration/specificity, and future-change fit. The four dimensions yield an idea score from 0 to 10; up to ten idea scores are summed to a participant total from 0 to 100, averaged across the raters. Similar or duplicate ideas within a participant and round incur novelty deductions. The analyzed outcome is the participant total in round two minus the total in round one. The recorded arm means and SDs are gain scores, not endpoint scores. Rater expertise is unstated, so human_raters is provisional. Scoring: PDF p. 5 (printed p. 44), Sections 3.2.1-3.2.3, and PDF p. 6 (printed p. 45), Sections 3.2.3-3.2.4.

stats.difference_is: Treatment mean gain minus control mean gain; each gain is round-two total minus round-one total, as printed.

regression.model: Linear mixed-effects model of participant-round rubric totals: score ~ time * round_two_group + (1 | participant), with round one and A1 as reference categories. The estimate is a planned contrast of changes between the named arms. All complete participants enter the model. A participant random intercept accounts for repeated observations; no robust or clustered-SE estimator is explicitly named. PDF p. 6 (printed p. 45), Section 3.3.4.

estimates.notes: This is a between-person randomized contrast of changes within an initial-condition stratum, not a randomized-order crossover; within_person is null. The arm statistics and the contrast refer to round-two minus round-one participant totals. The mixed-model SE and CI account for repeated participant measurements. The quoted Table 4 rows preserve the printed round-one, round-two, and gain statistics; the structured means and SDs use only the gain column. No between-arm standardized effect is printed; the Table 3 dz values are within-arm effects and are not substituted. The paper names this a main planned contrast but states no preregistration. The full initially unassisted stratum was randomized between B1 and B2. Both arms produced the baseline without AI, and B1 had AI during the scored upgrade. n_total is the printed count for initial group B, not the count for the entire mixed model.

estimates.notes: This is a between-person randomized contrast of changes within an initial-condition stratum, not a randomized-order crossover; within_person is null. The arm statistics and the contrast refer to round-two minus round-one participant totals. The mixed-model SE and CI account for repeated participant measurements. The quoted Table 4 rows preserve the printed round-one, round-two, and gain statistics; the structured means and SDs use only the gain column. No between-arm standardized effect is printed; the Table 3 dz values are within-arm effects and are not substituted. The paper names this a main planned contrast but states no preregistration. The full initially AI-assisted stratum was randomized between A1 and A2. Both arms produced the baseline with AI; A1 retained AI during the scored upgrade and A2 lost access. This answers with_ai. It is not the unassisted prior-AI versus never-AI comparison A2 versus B2, which crosses the initial groups and is excluded. n_total is the printed count for initial group A, not the count for the entire mixed model.

not_extracted.what: S2-O1: round-one total creativity, A (AI) versus B (no AI), H1
not_extracted.reason: Assignment to the initial A/B groups is not described as random. All explicit randomization statements concern the subsequent within-group split. Therefore this comparison does not meet the randomized-assistance requirement, despite printed means, SDs, Welch test, CI, and Cohen d. PDF p. 6 (printed p. 45), Section 4.2; allocation, PDF pp. 4-5 (printed pp. 43-44), Section 3.1. Screening study S2 is not an additional independent sample.

not_extracted.what: S2-O2: unassisted round-two total creativity, A2 (prior AI) versus B2 (never AI)
not_extracted.reason: This after_ai comparison crosses initial groups whose allocation is unstated; random splitting within A and B does not establish random prior-AI exposure between them. Only arm descriptives are printed, and no A2 versus B2 test is reported. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 46), Table 4; allocation, PDF p. 5 (printed p. 44), Section 3.1.

not_extracted.what: Round-one balance tests: A1 versus A2 and B1 versus B2
not_extracted.reason: Both arms in each pair had the same AI availability when the baseline outcome was produced. These are checks before the randomized switching intervention, not its effects. PDF p. 6 (printed p. 45), Section 3.3.1 and Table 1.

not_extracted.what: Pooled round-one to round-two total-creativity change, H2
not_extracted.reason: The paired comparison pools all AI histories and measures repetition/upgrade over time; it has no randomized AI-versus-comparison contrast. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 46), Section 4.3, Table 2 and Figure 2.

not_extracted.what: Within-arm paired changes for A1, A2, B1 and B2, and the A1 mixed-model time effect
not_extracted.reason: These compare successive task stages within a single arm. Task-stage order was fixed, not randomized, and these are not paired randomized-order AI contrasts. Table 3 paired tests and dz values, and the reference-arm time coefficient, must not be used as between-arm effects or uncertainty. PDF p. 7 (printed p. 46), Table 3 and Section 4.4.2.

not_extracted.what: Switching asymmetry, (B1 minus B2 gain) minus (A1 minus A2 gain), H5
not_extracted.reason: This compares the two treatment effects across initial-AI strata and is an effect-modification contrast, not an additional two-arm AI assistance contrast. Initial A/B assignment is also unstated. Excluded under the rule against moderation results. PDF p. 8 (printed p. 47), Section 4.4.2, item 3.

open_items: The paper does not report how students entered initial groups A and B; S2 contrasts cannot be treated as randomized.
Counts initially recruited, randomized, and excluded are not printed. The analysis includes only participants who completed both rounds; n_randomized remains null for the study and every arm.
Rater backgrounds are unstated. human_raters is provisional; expert_raters would apply if the raters were domain experts or instructors.
The specific ChatGPT model/version, its release year, collection dates, and actual uptake of alternative generative AI tools are not stated; ai_tool.year remains null.
The paper reports no arm-level idea counts, per-idea mean quality scores, or separate component effects, so quantity and quality cannot be separated in the summed creativity total.
No preregistration or posted data/supplement is identified. The paper reports planned main contrasts, but their preregistered-primary status cannot be established.
notes: Extraction by B on 2026-10-10. Read the entire ten-page PDF and all 524 lines of its markdown conversion; checked all tables with pymupdf, inspected all three figures, and confirmed every structured numerical result against PDF page text. No appendix, supplement, or embedded attachment is present or identified in the retrieval record. Figures reproduce tabulated descriptives and supply no additional extractable contrasts. The statistical inventory comprises baseline balance tests (Table 1), the initial A/B comparison (Section 4.2), pooled repetition descriptives and test (Table 2/Section 4.3), within-arm changes (Table 3), all arm baseline/endpoint/gain descriptives (Table 4), and the mixed-model reference-arm time effect and planned adoption, discontinuation, and asymmetry contrasts (Section 4.4.2). Only adoption and discontinuation meet the specified two-arm randomized-contrast scope. Their Table 4 source quotes retain every arm descriptive; structured means and SDs use the gain outcome that the paper tests. Both contrasts use all analyzed members of their separately randomized initial-condition strata, not post hoc subgroups. The mixed model is fitted to all analyzed students, while each estimate count covers only its two named arms. S1 and excluded screening S2 refer to the same students. No external sample overlap is identified in the form or paper. The paper describes an educational field experiment in actual IT-related classes, supporting field_rct rather than a separate laboratory setting. Country is inferred from the paper describing two domestic universities in this Korean study. The task was repeated in the same session with a break of about 30 minutes; there is no later-session follow-up, and no conversion of that interval into days was made. Random assignment is within initial A and B, not assignment of treatment order. A participant random intercept supports se_basis participant; the SE estimator itself is not otherwise named. The total mixes the quantity and rated quality of ideas. No diversity outcome is measured. No effects, counts, standard errors, or standardized effects were calculated from the printed numbers.
